questions.title: Full history and hidden state
questions.prompt: Consider a POMDP with a fixed environment model and initial distribution. A complete log contains every action, observation, and received reward, but an access flag has never been directly observed. Does uncertainty about the flag prevent the complete log from being a Markov information state? How does a belief state differ, and what can change when the log is truncated?
questions.explanation: It does not. Under these assumptions, the complete history $H_t$ determines the conditional distribution of the future and can serve as a growing Markov information state without identifying the hidden flag. The belief $b_t(s)=P(s_t=s\mid H_t)$ is a distribution over hidden states that summarizes history for prediction; it does not add a missing observation. A text log is not automatically an explicitly computed $b_t$. A truncated window or summary can discard relevant observations and therefore need not remain sufficient. Different hidden realizations compatible with one full history express uncertainty, not a violation of the Markov property.

questions.title: A controller-generated token sequence
questions.prompt: The model emits the symbolic action `OPEN_RED`, after which a controller serializes it into long JSON. Which tokens belong in the policy loss?
questions.explanation: If the model chose only the symbolic action, the learned action is `OPEN_RED` and its recorded probability. The JSON tokens were produced by a deterministic controller and receive no policy-gradient term. A stochastic serializer treated as part of a composite policy would need its own logged probability.

questions.title: Collector truncation
questions.prompt: A transition gives reward 0, the next value is 0.7, and $\gamma=0.9$. Collection stops, but the environment has not terminated. Compute the one-step critic target.
questions.explanation: Bootstrap through the collector boundary: $y=0+0.9\cdot0.7=0.63$. A zero target would correspond to true task termination or a separately declared no-continuation objective.

questions.title: Semantic action probability
questions.prompt: Two JSON strings parse to the same action and have probabilities 0.25 and 0.35. What is the semantic-action probability?
questions.explanation: The mutually exclusive serializations add: $0.25+0.35=0.60$. A standard token loss still scores the sampled string unless it explicitly sums over all equivalent serializations.

questions.title: Turn probability ratio
questions.prompt: The turn log-probability sums under current and behavior policies are $-2.1$ and $-2.4$. Compute the sequence ratio.
questions.explanation: $r=\exp[-2.1-(-2.4)]=e^{0.3}\approx1.34986$. Products across many turns can become heavy-tailed even when each local ratio looks modest.

questions.title: Synchronous straggler cost
questions.prompt: Four rollouts take 1, 1, 2, and 8 seconds. What is utilization for four synchronous workers?
questions.explanation: Useful work is 12 worker-seconds; batch capacity is $4\cdot8=32$. Utilization is $12/32=0.375$ and idle fraction is $0.625$. Module 12 develops the asynchronous systems consequences.

questions.title: Branching without a state snapshot
questions.prompt: An agent branches after a search call, but every branch queries the live search service again. Are the actions compared from one state?
questions.explanation: Not necessarily. Index contents, ranking, and hidden session state may differ. A local comparison requires a restorable snapshot or deterministic replay, fixed randomness, and the same shared prefix; otherwise action effects are confounded with environment differences.

questions.title: A homogeneous group
questions.prompt: All eight rewards in a rollout group equal 1. What remains after subtracting the group mean?
questions.explanation: Every relative advantage is zero. A larger learning rate cannot create missing variation. Change the task distribution, group design, or signal source. KL and entropy terms may still have gradients, but they are different signals.

questions.title: Repeatable inspect reward
questions.prompt: Why is $+0.1$ for every `inspect` more dangerous than a first-visit bonus?
questions.explanation: A repeatable bonus turns a loop into an independent source of return. First-visit payment limits repetition but still lacks the general invariance theorem. Potential-based shaping has a stricter form under its assumptions.

questions.title: What an agent benchmark measures
questions.prompt: A browser-controller replacement improves success without changing model weights. Can the gain be attributed to RL?
questions.explanation: No. The score entangles the model, controller, observation representation, budget, retries, environment, and verifier. Attribution requires ablations with a fixed execution contract.

questions.title: Online or offline first
questions.prompt: The environment sends real emails and has no safe reset. Which initial training route is preferable?
questions.explanation: Start with a simulator, shadow mode, expert logs, or state-conditioned offline preferences. Online RL with irreversible production actions is unacceptable without sandboxing, least privilege, and a confirmation protocol.

questions.title: Experiment passport
questions.prompt: Name at least six fields needed to reproduce a multi-turn rollout.
questions.explanation: At minimum: task/environment ID and version; initial state or seed; actions and observations; policy token IDs and provenance mask; behavior log-probabilities; policy version per turn; decoding settings; rewards and verifier version; stop reason with terminated/truncated/infra status; duration and cost. External tools make exact versions and state snapshots even more important.
